title: Endeavour Silver | Endeavour Silver Intersects 3,431 g/t Silver Equivalent over 1.42 Metres at Guanaceví; Multiple High-Grade Intercepts Highlight Contraria Vein Potential
summary: Endeavour Silver Corp. is a mid-tier precious metals mining company listed on the NYSE:EXK and TSX:EDR.
body_markdown:
**VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Endeavour Silver Corp. (“Endeavour” or the “Company”)** **(TSX: EDR, NYSE: EXK)** is pleased to announce high-grade drill results from its 2026 exploration program at the Guanaceví mine in Durango, Mexico. The 20-hole, 5,855-metre program tested the Santa Cruz vein system and nearby parallel structures at Alondra-P2 and El Milache, returning multiple high-grade silver-gold intersections.


Drilling at Alondra-P2 was highlighted by three Contraria vein intersections exceeding 1,000 grams per tonne (g/t) silver equivalent (AgEq) over approximately one metre or greater true width. UAP-03 returned 3,431 g/t AgEq over 1.42 m true width, including 14,878 g/t AgEq over 0.12 m, while UAP-08 and UAP-06 returned 1,736 g/t AgEq over 1.21 m and 1,296 g/t AgEq over 1.01 m, respectively. At El Milache, drilling intersected high-grade mineralization in the Santa Cruz vein as well as parallel footwall and hanging-wall structures, highlighting multiple targets for ongoing exploration and evaluation.


Key highlights from this program include:


- **UAP-03 (Contraria):** 11.21 g/t gold and 2,479 g/t silver (3,431 g/t AgEq), over 1.42 metres (m) true width, including 60.90 g/t gold and 9,701 g/t silver (14,878 g/t AgEq) over 0.12 m
- **UAP-08 (Contraria):** 3.36 g/t gold and 1,451 g/t silver (1,736 g/t AgEq) over 1.21 m true width, including 9.19 g/t gold and 3,809 g/t silver (4,590 g/t AgEq) over 0.29 m
- **UMH-09 (Santa Cruz):** 3.69 g/t gold and 1,335 g/t silver (1,648 g/t AgEq) over 0.89 m true width, including 6.58 g/t gold and 2,375 g/t silver (2,934 g/t AgEq) over 0.23 m
- **UAP-06 (Contraria):** 1.15 g/t gold and 1,198 g/t silver (1,296 g/t AgEq) over 1.01 m true width, including 2.18 g/t gold and 2,058 g/t silver (2,243 g/t AgEq) over 0.26 m
- **UMH-04 (FW Santa Cruz):** 1.80 g/t gold and 817 g/t silver (970 g/t AgEq) over 0.93 m true width, including 4.04 g/t gold and 1,912 g/t silver (2,255 g/t AgEq) over 0.36 m
- **UMH-04 (Santa Cruz):** 1.26 g/t gold and 334 g/t silver (441 g/t AgEq) over 2.32 m true width


“These results reinforce the quality of the vein systems at Guanaceví and the strength of our exploration pipeline,” said Dan Dickson, Chief Executive Officer. “The high grades in the Contraria vein, combined with consistent mineralization along the Santa Cruz structure, give us added confidence as we work to extend mine life and continue delivering value from this cornerstone operation.”


**Contraria Vein:**


Five of the eight UAP-series holes intersected the Contraria vein, with true widths ranging from 1.01 m to 1.42 m. Drilling at Alondra-P2 returned significant mineralization from the Contraria vein in five holes, including three intercepts grading more than 1,000 g/t AgEq across true widths of approximately one metre or greater. UAP-03 returned the highest-grade composite in the program at 3,431 g/t AgEq over 1.42 m true width, while UAP-08 and UAP-06 returned 1,736 g/t AgEq over 1.21 m and 1,296 g/t AgEq over 1.01 m, respectively. The consistency of the high-grade intersections across multiple holes provides compelling support for further evaluation of Contraria as a potentially meaningful additional mineralized structure within the Alondra-P2 area.


**Santa Cruz Vein System:**


At El Milache, drilling demonstrates that high-grade mineralization is not restricted to the principal Santa Cruz vein. UMH-04 intersected 970 g/t AgEq over 0.93 m true width in the footwall structure before intersecting 441 g/t AgEq over 2.32 m in Santa Cruz. Similarly, UMH-09 returned 1,648 g/t AgEq over 0.89 m in Santa Cruz and 352 g/t AgEq over 1.24 m in a hanging-wall structure. These results highlight the potential for multiple mineralized veins within the broader Santa Cruz vein system and identify additional targets that warrant evaluation in future drilling and mine planning.

**About Endeavour Silver**


Endeavour is a mid-tier silver producer with three operating mines in Mexico and Peru and a robust pipeline of exploration projects across Mexico, Chile, and the United States. With a proven track record of discovery, development, and responsible mining, Endeavour is driving organic growth and creating lasting value on its path to becoming a leading senior silver producer.


**Qualified Person and Data Verification**


The scientific and technical information in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Dale Mah, P.Geo., VP Corporate Development of Endeavour Silver, a “Qualified Person” as defined by National Instrument 43-101 Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”). Mr. Mah is an employee of the Company and is not independent of the Company.


Dale Mah, P.Geo., has verified the data disclosed in this news release, including the sampling, analytical and test data underlying the information, by reviewing drill logs, sample intervals and the laboratory certificates of analysis, and reviewing the QA/QC results for the reference standards, blanks and duplicates, which were within acceptable limits. There were no limitations on, or failures to complete, the verification process.


**QA/QC and Analytical Procedures**


A quality assurance and quality control (“QA/QC”) program of certified reference standards, blanks and duplicates is applied to monitor the integrity of all assay results. Core is logged and cut/split at the Company’s Durango, Mexico facility, and samples are shipped to SGS, Durango, Mexico, where they are dried, crushed, split and a 250-gram pulp is prepared for analysis. Gold is assayed by 30-gram fire assay with atomic absorption (“AA”) finish and silver by aqua regia digestion with ICP-OES finish; over-limit samples are re-assayed by fire assay with gravimetric finish. SGS is independent of the Company and is ISO/IEC 17025 accredited.
